summary: Yuka Otani works in Buddhist studies. Her career includes attested part-time lecturer positions at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University in 2015.

Yukari Kimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having completed doctoral studies under Kenyu Mitomo. She is attested as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University via the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute in 2026.

Yukei Matsunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Koyasan, Tohoku, and Kyushu universities. He served as Director at Koyasan University in 1983 and held a post at Shuchiin University around 2001 to 2007.

Yuki Kyogoku is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied as a doctoral student at the University of Leipzig. He worked at Accenture (2013–2014) and as a research associate at the University of Leipzig in 2018.

Yuki Sasaki is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 2026, Sasaki is attested as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yuki Shibuya works in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Tokyo (2016–2018), where he also held an appointment as a project research fellow in 2014.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015). Takatsukasa also served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held a professorship at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and served as a Ministry of Education overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).
Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015), where he also served as a specialist researcher (attested 2026).

Yukihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn. He served as associate professor and professor emeritus at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College and adviser at Minobusan University.
Yukihisa Yamao was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from around 1954 to 1963 and later held an academic post there from circa 1974 to 2001.

Yukio Hattori was a scholar of Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University from around 1951 to 1955 and later held a post at Japan Women's University from circa 1991 to 2001.

Yukio Kotani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. He served as professor emeritus of comparative literature at Rissho University, where he held an appointment from circa 1970 to 2002.

Yukio Sakamoto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University. He served as professor and president at Rissho University, directed its Lotus Sutra institute, and was a professor at Toyo University (ca. 1961–1970).

Yukio Takeda was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1964). He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1964–1970), Nagoya City University (~1970–1977), the University of Tokyo (~1977–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~1998–2005).

Yukio Yamanaka is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and earned a PhD from the University of Freiburg. Appointments include DFG Research Fellow at Göttingen (attested 2015) and a post at Ryukoku University.

Yuko Kamishima works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, having studied at Indiana, Cambridge, and Tokyo universities. She served as an assistant at Waseda University (2006–2016) and became a professor at Ritsumeikan University in 2016.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College. She held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She served as an associate professor at Kyoto University (attested 2002–2021).
Yulian Zeng specializes in Buddhist studies. Zeng studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under supervisor Kirill Solonin, and also studied under the traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
